</row>

**Access** A character who is a member of the Knights of Lastwall has access to this option.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

_Sinister knight_ armor shrouds the wearer’s identity in secrecy, allowing Crimson Reclaimers to pass among foes without being immediately unmasked. The wearer gains a +1 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision;     **Effect** With a thought, the wearer activates a disguise. While the _sinister knight_ armor’s disguise is active, any identifying insignia or aesthetic of the armor is replaced by generic malevolent aesthetics such as spikes or demonic faces. While in the disguise, the wearer is always considered to be taking precautions against [lifesense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=21), and even a creature that successfully notices the wearer with its lifesense mistakes the wearer for an undead unless it critically succeeds at its Perception check or the wearer critically fails a Deception or [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) check. Finally, while in the disguise, the rune attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=299) any effects that would reveal your alignment; on a successful counteract check, rather than negate the effect, the rune causes the effect to perceive your alignment as evil (maintaining any lawful or chaotic component of your alignment).

 The wearer can [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=74) the disguise, and if the wearer’s armor is removed, the disguise deactivates automatically.

May contain spoilers from Blood Lords **Source** [Pathfinder #183: Field of Maidens](/Sources.aspx?ID=145) pg. 79 --- Sisterstone is a term used for two closely related ores infused by the spiritual runoff in the Field of Maidens, dusk sisterstone and scarlet sisterstone. They have the same physical properties except for color—dusk sisterstone is a pale orange while scarlet sisterstone is orange-red. When near an object made of the other type of sisterstone, they both begin exuding spiritual energy that repels [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160). When an object made of dusk sisterstone is within 15 feet of an object made of scarlet sisterstone of the same grade, they create a reciprocal field. Any undead creature adjacent to one of the objects when the field is formed, or who moves adjacent to one while the field is active, becomes [enfeebled 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13) unless it succeeds at a DC 15 Fortitude save. This lasts until the undead creature is no longer adjacent to either of the items or until the field's removed (typically by the objects ceasing to be within 15 feet of one another). The DC increases to 22 if both items are standard grade or better, and to 33 if they're both high grade. Unworked chunks and ingots don't create a reciprocal field. A single object can't be made of both types of sisterstone. ## Sisterstone Items

May contain spoilers from Blood Lords **Source** [Pathfinder #183: Field of Maidens](/Sources.aspx?ID=145) pg. 79 --- Sisterstone is a term used for two closely related ores infused by the spiritual runoff in the Field of Maidens, dusk sisterstone and scarlet sisterstone. They have the same physical properties except for color—dusk sisterstone is a pale orange while scarlet sisterstone is orange-red. When near an object made of the other type of sisterstone, they both begin exuding spiritual energy that repels [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160). When an object made of dusk sisterstone is within 15 feet of an object made of scarlet sisterstone of the same grade, they create a reciprocal field. Any undead creature adjacent to one of the objects when the field is formed, or who moves adjacent to one while the field is active, becomes [enfeebled 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13) unless it succeeds at a DC 15 Fortitude save. This lasts until the undead creature is no longer adjacent to either of the items or until the field's removed (typically by the objects ceasing to be within 15 feet of one another). The DC increases to 22 if both items are standard grade or better, and to 33 if they're both high grade. Unworked chunks and ingots don't create a reciprocal field. A single object can't be made of both types of sisterstone. ## Sisterstone Items

A weapon with a sisterstone striking surface can be charged with [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160)-destroying energy in response to violence from an undead creature. A creature wielding a sisterstone weapon gains the following activation. Only melee weapons can be made of sisterstone.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> command;   **Trigger** The ally is critically hit by a Strike from an undead creature you can see; **Requirements** A reciprocal field is active between this weapon and an ally's sisterstone armor or sisterstone weapon; **Effect** Your weapon leaps out with positive energy in retaliation. Strike the triggering undead with the weapon, and your Strike deals 2 additional positive damage. The positive damage increases to 4 if your sisterstone weapon is standard grade, or 6 if it's high grade. If the triggering undead is beyond the reach of your sisterstone weapon, your Strike doesn't deal its base damage, but can still deal the positive damage.

**Bulk**  varies by weapon

<row gap="medium">

**Base Material** [Sisterstone](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1720)

</column>

---

A weapon with a sisterstone striking surface can be charged with [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160)-destroying energy in response to violence from an undead creature. A creature wielding a sisterstone weapon gains the following activation. Only melee weapons can be made of sisterstone.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> command;   **Trigger** The ally is critically hit by a Strike from an undead creature you can see; **Requirements** A reciprocal field is active between this weapon and an ally's sisterstone armor or sisterstone weapon; **Effect** Your weapon leaps out with positive energy in retaliation. Strike the triggering undead with the weapon, and your Strike deals 2 additional positive damage. The positive damage increases to 4 if your sisterstone weapon is standard grade, or 6 if it's high grade. If the triggering undead is beyond the reach of your sisterstone weapon, your Strike doesn't deal its base damage, but can still deal the positive damage.

[Heartstone](/Equipment.aspx?ID=487)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Bestiary](/Sources.aspx?ID=2) pg. 203

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This gemstone grants its wearer a +2 item bonus to saving throws.

Each _heartstone_ is powered by the spirit of a specific night hag. If it’s separated from her for 24 hours (or she’s been dead for 24 hours), it becomes a nonmagical gemstone. A _heartstone_ allows the hag to use additional occult innate spells: _[ethereal jaunt](/Spells.aspx?ID=105)_ (9th level) and _[bind soul](/Spells.aspx?ID=21)_ at will, and _[shadow blast](/Spells.aspx?ID=273)_ twice per day.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command;    **Requirements** You must be touching the _heartstone_.; **Effect** The _heartstone_ attempts to counteract one disease affecting you (counteract level 5, counteract modifier +18).

**Craft Requirements** You must be a night hag.

</title>

---

This pale gemstone grants its wearer a +2 item bonus to saving throws and the ability to discern a target's alignment (as [_detect alignment_](/Spells.aspx?ID=65), but can detect chaotic, evil, good, and lawful auras simultaneously) at will by peering through the gemstone.

 Like all hag _heartstones_, this gemstone is powered by [Skarja's](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2110) spirit. Skarja does not need to wear her _heartstone_ to benefit from its powers, but she cannot use them if she hasn't touched her _heartstone_ in the past 7 days. If Skarja's _heartstone_ is separated from her for more than 7 days (or if she's been dead for 7 days), it becomes a non-magical gemstone. Skarja's _heartstone_ allows her to use additional occult innate spells: [_ethereal jaunt_](/Spells.aspx?ID=105) (9th level) and [_bind soul_](/Spells.aspx?ID=21) at will, [_shadow blast_](/Spells.aspx?ID=273) (6th level) twice per day, and [_spirit blast_](/Spells.aspx?ID=301) once per day.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command;    **Requirements** You must be touching the _heartstone_; **Effect** The _heartstone_ attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) one [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46) affecting you (counteract level 7, counteract modifier +23).

---

This _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [tekko-kagi](/Weapons.aspx?ID=101)_ resembles a clawed skeletal hand that fits over your own. Embedded in the back of the bony hand is an onyx gemstone held in place by fine silver chains. When the claws tear into a living creature, the gem pulses with negative energy. The _skeletal claw_ deals an additional 1d4 [persistent negative damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) to living creatures (1d10 persistent negative damage on a critical hit).

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> command;  **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You cast a spell to summon an [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) creature that has a skeletal structure, such as with [_animate dead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=666);  **Effect** The triggering undead creature has 10 temporary Hit Points that last for 1 minute. As long as any of these temporary Hit Points remain, the _skeletal claw_ doesn't deal additional negative damage.

A grinning skull tops the bow of this macabre key. [Skinsaw Mask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2354)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Unholy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=521" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 155, [Pathfinder #158: Sixty Feet Under](/Sources.aspx?ID=47) pg. 76

**Price** 50 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn mask

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A patchwork of [humanoid](/Traits.aspx?ID=628) flesh makes up a _skinsaw mask_, which is stitched together with black silk or wire. It is distinctive for its bulbous orange eye—crafted from a magical glass bauble—and wide row of teeth. When worn, the mask amplifies your ability to sense fear in other creatures. You know the value of the [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) condition of any observed creature, and you gain a +1 item bonus to [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2298) checks to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) frightened creatures. Whenever you deal precision damage to a frightened creature, you deal 1 additional precision damage. If you aren’t [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521), you are [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) 2 while wearing a _skinsaw mask_.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=528" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=564" />
<trait label="Healing" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=623" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 296

**Price** 55 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This sticky salve stubbornly holds wounds closed and encourages swift natural healing. You can activate the salve in either of the following ways.

**Activate—Administer Stitch** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** You [Administer First Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=2396) without requiring healer's tools. You can either gain a +2 item bonus to the [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42) check or use the salve's Medicine modifier of +13 instead of your own.

**Activate—Stitch Wounds** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))  **Trigger** You [Treat Wounds](/Actions.aspx?ID=2399) or use [Battle Medicine](/Feats.aspx?ID=5125);  **Effect** You gain a +2 item bonus to the triggering [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42) check. If you roll a success on the Medicine check, you get a critical success instead.

</column>

>
[Skirmisher's Coat](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3696)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Spore War</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #210: Whispers in the Dirt](/Sources.aspx?ID=253) pg. 79

**Price** 1,300 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn garment

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Valued among soldiers (particularly those from wartorn Nirmathas) who often find themselves operating undercover, this large-collared garment is reminiscent of a highwayman’s coat. A skirmisher’s coat is cleverly constructed, and contains several concealed pockets and grants the wearer a +2 item bonus to checks made to [Conceal an Object](/Actions.aspx?ID=2403).

**Activate—Costume Change** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=629))    **Effect** You change the shape and appearance of all your clothing, making them appear as ordinary or fine clothes of your imagining. This doesn’t change the statistics of any armor you’re wearing. Only a creature that’s benefiting from [_truesight_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1727) or a similar effect can attempt to disbelieve this illusion, with a DC of 28.

**Activate—Unexpected Armament** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You reach into one of the coat’s pockets and withdraw a chunk of metal that instantly expands into a common simple or martial melee weapon of your choice. The weapon functions as a _[+1 striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) weapon_. When you produce the weapon, you decide if it is made from [cold iron](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2916) or [silver](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2920), and which one of the following property runes it gains: [corrosive](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2834), [flaming](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2838), [frost](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2839), [shock](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2847), or [thundering](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2850). This weapon remains for 1 hour or until it leaves your grasp, at which point it vanishes.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #201: Pactbreaker](/Sources.aspx?ID=241) pg. 81

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** affixed to armor

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Free Action" /><row>envision</row></row>

 

**Trigger** You are [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=69) at the beginning of your turn.

 
</row>

</column>

---

Carved from an [arboreal’s](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=364) knuckle, this wooden torus can be activated despite your being unconscious. The knot then sprouts several roots that arch over your body like a spider’s legs. These lift you a few inches off the ground before [Striding](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) and carrying you with them. The roots prioritize taking you away from obvious harm, though as a reaction, an ally who speaks [Arboreal](/Languages.aspx?ID=26) can command the roots to carry you to a particular point within range. 

After moving, the roots continue protecting you; this counts as [Raising a Shield](/Actions.aspx?ID=2316), giving you a +1 circumstance bonus to AC until the beginning of your next turn. The roots use the [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=5212) reaction against the first physical attack against you, after which the roots crumble.

</column>

>
[Skittering Mask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2355)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 155, [Pathfinder #169: Kindled Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=94) pg. 74

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn mask

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A _skittering mask_ is a hand-carved, wooden, full-head mask that sports several holes along each side of the face. The first time each day that you begin your turn [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38) and within 25 feet of an enemy, skittering metallic insect legs emerge from the holes in the mask and Step 5 feet away from the nearest enemy, dragging your body along with the mask. If more than one enemy is equidistant, the mask Steps away from one of them at random. The mask possesses no special senses and does not react to [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) or [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39) enemies, nor can it distinguish that a creature not acting openly hostile is an enemy.

</column>

**Bulk** 1

</row>

</column>

---

The mask Steps 15 feet instead of 5 feet, and for 1 minute, each time you begin your turn unconscious and within 25 feet of an enemy, the mask Steps 15 feet away from the nearest enemy again. An ally can signal the mask with a single action, which has the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16) and [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) traits. If the mask hears the signal, it attempts to move you towards that ally when it Steps away from the nearest enemy.

---

This device is a human-sized skull crafted entirely from metal plating and clockwork gears, which slots easily into a human [skeleton](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=92) in the spot where an ordinary skull would normally be located. While performing a [_create undead_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=10) ritual, you can attach this skull bomb to the target creature in place of its own head. In order to do so, the target creature must be Medium and have the [humanoid](/Traits.aspx?ID=91) trait. The target creature can have only one skull bomb attached in this fashion. The creature gains the following ability.

 **Throw Skull** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) The creature detaches its skull bomb and hurls the volatile explosive at a point within 30 feet. The skull explodes, dealing 7d6 fire damage to creatures within a 15-foot burst (DC 24 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). The skull is permanently destroyed and can't be used again, and the throwing creature is permanently [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1) and headless.

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 45 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L **Activate**Strike --- Skunk bombs are made from the concentrated odors of [xulgaths](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=102), [hezrous](/Monsters.aspx?ID=601), and other creatures with natural or supernatural stench. The bomb grants an item bonus to attack rolls and deals poison damage and poison splash damage. Any creature hit by the bomb or in its splash area must attempt a Fortitude saving throw with a DC based on the bomb's type. Creatures in the splash area treat the results of their saving throw as one step better. **Critical Success** The target is unaffected.
**Success** The target is [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34).
**Failure** The target is sickened 1 and [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) while sickened.
**Critical Failure** The target is [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1) for 1 round, sickened 2, and slowed 1 while sickened. Creatures sickened by the bomb emit an odor that lasts 10 minutes after the sickened condition ends (or 1 hour if they were also blinded). The odor can be removed or neutralized by using [_prestidigitation_](/Spells.aspx?ID=229) or similar magic or by spending 10 minutes scrubbing with ample soap and water. While the odor lasts, creatures within 30 feet can smell the target, enabling even those with a weak sense of smell to detect its presence, and all creatures gain a +1 item bonus to [Track](/Actions.aspx?ID=66) the affected creature for as long as it has the odor. A creature that has [imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412) or [precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411) [scent](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=33) doubles the range at which it can detect the target using this scent. Skunk Bomb (Lesser) **Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 45 **Price** 4 gp **Bulk** L --- The bomb deals 1d4 poison damage and 1 poison splash damage. The Fortitude DC is 15. Skunk Bomb (Moderate) **Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 45 **Price** 12 gp **Bulk** L --- You gain a +1 item bonus to attack rolls. The bomb deals 2d4 poison damage and 2 poison splash damage. The Fortitude DC is 17. Skunk Bomb (Greater) **Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 45 **Price** 240 gp **Bulk** L --- You gain a +2 item bonus to attack rolls. The bomb deals 3d4 poison damage and 3 poison splash damage. The Fortitude DC is 28. Skunk Bomb (Major) **Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 45 **Price** 2,400 gp **Bulk** L --- You gain a +3 item bonus to attack rolls. The bomb deals 4d4 poison damage and 4 poison splash damage. The Fortitude DC is 37.

This azure bolt is carved in the shape of an undulating snake, its bared fangs framing the point of its head. When an activated _sky serpent bolt_ successfully hits a target, the bolt takes the form of a snake made of pure lightning, dealing 2d12 electricity damage to all creatures in a 30-foot line (DC 19 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save) starting from the target.

 If you spent 2 actions to activate the _sky serpent bolt_, then the line is 60 feet long, and at a single point in the line, you can change the remainder of the line's path by up to a 90-degree angle.

Large turquoise gems stud the outer edge of this sturdy _+3 [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [ghost touch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=297) [composite shortbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=75)_. Arrows shot from the bow are unimpaired by wind and air effects.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact ([conjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=33), [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=156))
 **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You shoot an arrow at an open space on a surface within 500 feet and momentarily vanish into a wind that carries the arrow. You teleport to that location.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, Interact ([electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=56))
 **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You shoot an arrow at the sky and it tears an extraplanar rift that resembles a storm cloud in a 30-foot burst centered on a point within 200 feet. A torrent of rain pours down from the rift for 1 minute or until you Dismiss the effect. The area within the torrent becomes difficult terrain for all movement (including [Flying](/Actions.aspx?ID=94)). As an Interact action, you can fire an arrow into the rift to cause a bolt of lightning to strike a creature in the area. The creature takes 5d12 lightning damage and must attempt a DC 41 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes (command, envision, Interact);  **Frequency** once per week;   **Effect** You fire a volley of arrows into the sky. You create the effects of a successful [_control weather_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=9) ritual.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 11"
    pfs=""
>
[Skyfang Crystal](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3175)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #199: To Bloom Below the Web](/Sources.aspx?ID=225) pg. 77

**Price** 2,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A _skyfang crystal_ appears as a softly glowing length of blue crystal shaped like a gently curved fang; it's typically affixed to a short length of chain, allowing it to be worn as a necklace or wrapped around a forearm. The light it sheds is equal in strength to that of a candle; it can't be extinguished but can be blocked simply by wrapping the crystal in cloth, wearing it under clothing, or keeping it in a container. The first of these magical crystals was believed to have been created by a dying sky dragon who'd spent her life fighting against evil spirits. She plucked a dozen of her smallest teeth from her jaw and offered them to her 12 most trusted allies so that they could continue to track down evil spirits and remain protected as they did so, even after she was gone. A _skyfang crystal_ provides illumination as a candle that can't be extinguished, and as long as you have it invested, you gain mental resistance 10. If you're evil, you're enfeebled 2 while you have a _skyfang crystal_ invested. 

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You touch the _skyfang crystal_ to your brow and utter the name of a specific fiend or spirit you seek. If the target is on the same plane as you, the _skyfang crystal_ pulses stronger with light when you face in the approximate direction of the named creature, allowing you to [Track](/Actions.aspx?ID=2408) that creature. The DC for this check is equal to the creature's Will DC, and you can use Occultism, Religion, or Survival to attempt the check. As long as you're tracking this fiend or spirit, you gain a +2 item bonus to saving throws against effects that creature generates. This effect persists until you activate the _skyfang crystal_ again to track a different target

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

_Skyfisher vapors_ are only visible via their effect on a [_toxic cloud_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1722) spell, or apparent lack thereof. Your magical connection to the cloud means you always know where it is. This has no effect on its damage.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command;  **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** You're holding the sword in at least one hand; **Effect** You leap upon your sword as it soars through the air for up to 10 minutes. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 276

**Price** 2,450 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This matched pair of slates, roughly one handspan wide and tall, have identical ornate frames. Slates are crafted in pairs, and each works with only the other of its pair. If one slate of a pair is ever broken, the other shatters into non-magical shards. The listed price is for a pair of slates. 

**Activate—Send a Message** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You use a piece of chalk to write up to 25 words on a slate. This dull red stone is shot through with glittering veins of black and silver. When you apply a _slayer’s stone_ to your weapon, choose [aberration](/Traits.aspx?ID=523), [animal](/Traits.aspx?ID=531), [beast](/Traits.aspx?ID=547), [celestial](/Traits.aspx?ID=551), [construct](/Traits.aspx?ID=563), [dragon](/Traits.aspx?ID=581), [elemental](/Traits.aspx?ID=587), [fey](/Traits.aspx?ID=599), [fiend](/Traits.aspx?ID=600), [giant](/Traits.aspx?ID=616), [monitor](/Traits.aspx?ID=655), [ooze](/Traits.aspx?ID=665), or both [fungus](/Traits.aspx?ID=614) and [plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=668). A weapon under the effect of a _slayer’s stone_ deals an additional 1d6 precision damage to the creatures with the chosen trait or traits for 1 minute. It’s up to the GM’s discretion whether this benefit applies against a creature disguised as a creature with the chosen trait or traits.

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 296 **Usage** worn garment **Bulk** L --- This loose robe has wide, voluminous sleeves that each contain an extradimensional space. These spaces each function as a spacious pouch that can hold up to 5 Bulk of items (for a total of 10 Bulk), though no individual item can be of more than 1 Bulk; the sleeves grow slightly heavy as you reach maximum capacity. You can add or remove an item from a sleeve with a single hand free as an Interact action.
If a sleeve is completely empty, you can place your own familiar into that extradimensional space. It can survive comfortably in your sleeve for up to 1 hour, after which it begins to suffocate. While in your sleeve, it can't be affected or targeted by any effects, but you don't benefit from any master abilities. A familiar can exit the sleeve of its own volition with a single action that has the manipulate and move traits. You can't place any other creature into your sleeves, nor can you place your familiar in a sleeve if it's larger than Tiny. If your familiar is in your sleeve, you can't place any items in the sleeve. Sleeves of Storage **Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 296, [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 263 **Price** 100 gp Sleeves of Storage (Greater) **Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 296, [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 263 **Price** 600 gp --- Each sleeve can hold up to 20 Bulk of items, and a familiar can survive within a sleeve for up to 4 hours.

This loose robe has wide, voluminous sleeves that each contain an extradimensional space. These spaces each function as a [_bag of holding_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=249) that can hold up to 5 Bulk of items (for a total of 10 Bulk), though no individual item can be of more than 1 Bulk; the sleeves grow slightly heavy as you reach maximum capacity. You can add or remove an item from a sleeve with a single hand free as an Interact action.

 If a sleeve is completely empty, you can place your own familiar into that extradimensional space. It can survive comfortably in your sleeve for up to 1 hour, after which it begins to [suffocate](/Rules.aspx?ID=468). While in your sleeve, it can't be affected or targeted by any effects, but you don't benefit from any master abilities. A familiar can exit the sleeve of its own volition with a single action that has the [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104) and [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=114) traits. You can't place any other creature into your sleeves, nor can you place your familiar in a sleeve if it's larger than Tiny. If your familiar is in your sleeve, you can't place any items in the sleeve.

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 205 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L --- A famed detective once owned the long, curved _sleuth's pipe_, taking it with them on investigations, keeping it in hand or mouth while cogitating. The pipe might have passed down through generations. Or, when an owner dies without heirs, it could go up for auction, be given to family friends, or remain at the scene of a crime to be found later. The _sleuth's pipe_ has sapience that eventually awakens, allowing the relic to act as a helpful assistant in investigations. Even while this sapience sleeps within the pipe, it grants you a +1 item bonus to Perception checks to [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=85), and if you're an [investigator](/Classes.aspx?ID=13), any checks you make to [Pursue a Lead](/Actions.aspx?ID=544). --- **Minor Gifts**: [beginner's luck](/Relics.aspx?ID=97), [repository of knowledge](/Relics.aspx?ID=51)
**Major Gifts**: [intelligent relic](/Relics.aspx?ID=109), [steal luck](/Relics.aspx?ID=101)
**Grand Gift**: [mental bastion](/Relics.aspx?ID=54)

</title>

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

---

This thick, greasy _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [shifting](/Equipment.aspx?ID=302) [whip](/Weapons.aspx?ID=48)_ is made from a slimy pseudopod. You don't take the usual –2 circumstance penalty to your attack rolls when using the slime whip to make a lethal attack. The whip's form can be changed just like any weapon with the _shifting_ rune, but it reverts to its original form as soon as it isn't wielded. When in its whip form, you can use the following action.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command, Interact;  **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** For 1 round, the slime whip deals acid damage rather than slashing damage. If the attack deals [persistent damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29), the persistent damage is also acid damage instead of its usual type.

[Slippers of Spider Climbing](/Equipment.aspx?ID=465)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 616

**Price** 325 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn shoes

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These soft slippers are made of fine gray silk. If the slippers are left unattended for a while, they tend to attract spiders that nest inside.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command;  **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** Tiny, hairlike tendrils extend from the slippers’ soles, allowing you to walk on vertical surfaces or even to move upside down along ceilings. For 1 minute, you gain a 20-foot climb Speed and you don’t need to use your hands to Climb. However, the slippers require decent traction for you to walk on a wall, so they provide no benefit when you’re moving across greased, icy, or oiled surfaces.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 15"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Slithermaw's Bane](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3700)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Spore War</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #211: The Secret of Deathstalk Tower](/Sources.aspx?ID=254) pg. 82

**Price** 6,500 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Chain Shirt](/Armor.aspx?ID=6)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This suit of _[+2 greater resilient ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2804) [elven chain](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2801)_ was worn by the elven hero Kyloss Syndar. The armor served him well, but eventually he fell in battle against the demonic hydra Slithermaw. As Kyloss slew the demonic beast, its fangs pierced his chest and mortally wounded the elf. The armor retains several ragged holes along the chest and abdomen where the hydra’s teeth damaged it. 

_Slithermaw’s Bane_ grants its wearer poison [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) 10, and the [resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2786) rune increases the item bonus on saving throws versus [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) by 1 (to +3).

**Activate—Calistria’s Sting** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** A creature [grapples](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376) you;  **Effect** Poison wells up from the armor’s links to seep into the triggering creature’s body, causing it to suffer wracking pains as if it were being stung by thousands of angry wasps. The triggering creature takes 7d6 [persistent poison damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) (DC 34 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2247) Fortitude save); this persistent damage cannot be ended as long as the triggering creature continues to grapple you.

**Activate—Terrain Adaptation** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You alter the exterior of the armor to better adapt to the surrounding [terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=3108): [aquatic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2770), [arctic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2773), [desert](/Rules.aspx?ID=2776), [forest](/Rules.aspx?ID=2779), [mountain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2783), [plains](/Rules.aspx?ID=2789), sky, [swamp](/Rules.aspx?ID=2792), or [underground](/Rules.aspx?ID=2808). You ignore non-magical [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366) within the chosen environment and gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against [environmental hazards](/Rules.aspx?ID=2588), [natural disasters](/Rules.aspx?ID=2823), and [extreme temperatures](/Rules.aspx?ID=2820) that originate from that terrain. You are also protected from severe and extreme heat or severe and extreme cold (your choice when you activate this ability). This effect lasts until your next [daily preparation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>
[Slithermaw's Bane (Artifact)](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3753)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Spore War</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="No Alignment" url="/Rules.aspx?ID=95" />
<trait label="Apex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=10" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Intelligent" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=280" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #212: A Voice in the Blight](/Sources.aspx?ID=255) pg. 73

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Perception** +34; precise [low-light vision](/Rules.aspx?ID=2411) and hearing within 30 feet

**Communication** [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) (partner only)

**Skills** [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) +35, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +33, [Warfare Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) +33

**Int** +5, **Wis** +6, **Cha** +7

**Will** +34 

</column>

---        

The heroism of Kyloss Syndar, founder of Greengold and slayer of the demonic hydra Slithermaw, imprinted this suit of armor with a gleaming, prismatic sheen that sparkles under bright light. The telepathic voice of _Slithermaw’s Bane_ is boisterous and grandiose, encouraging his partner to take up leadership roles while also providing advice to maintain loyalty and strengthen bonds of friendship. 

_Slithermaw’s Bane_ is a suit of _[+3 major resilient ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2804) [greater fortification](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2789) high-grade [elven chain](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2801)_ that grants his wearer poison [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) 15, and the item bonus his resilient rune grants to saving throws versus poison increases by 1 to +4.

**Activate—Calistria’s Sting** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** A creature [grapples](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376) you;  **Effect** Poison wells up from the armor’s links to seep into the triggering creature’s body, causing it to suffer wracking pains as if it was being stung by thousands of angry wasps. The triggering creature takes 7d6 [persistent poison damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) (DC 34 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2247) Fortitude save); this persistent damage can’t be ended as long as the triggering creature continues to grapple you. _Slithermaw’s Bane_ can’t activate [Calistria’s](/Deities.aspx?ID=279) Sting using his actions.

**Activate—Purge Toxins** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** _Slithermaw’s Bane_ attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) a [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578) or [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) [affliction](/Rules.aspx?ID=2389) affecting you, with a counteract rank of 9th and a +25 modifier to the roll (+30 modifier if the source of the disease or poison effect on you was created by a [fiend](/Traits.aspx?ID=600)).

**Activate—Adaptation** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You alter the exterior of the armor to better adapt to the surrounding [terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2365): [aquatic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2770), [arctic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2773), [desert](/Rules.aspx?ID=2776), [forest](/Rules.aspx?ID=2779), [mountain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2783), [plains](/Rules.aspx?ID=2789), sky, [swamp](/Rules.aspx?ID=2792), or [underground](/Rules.aspx?ID=2808). You [ignore difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2367) within the chosen [environment](/Rules.aspx?ID=590) and gain a +2 circumstance bonus to saving throws against [environmental hazards](/Rules.aspx?ID=2588), [natural disasters](/Rules.aspx?ID=2823), and extreme temperatures that originate from that terrain. You’re also protected from [severe and extreme heat or severe and extreme cold](/Rules.aspx?ID=2820) (your choice when you activate this ability). This effect lasts until your next daily preparations or the next time you activate it, whichever comes first.

_Nethys Note: the non-artifact version of the item is [here.](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3700) This artifact's heroic legacy, and its subsequent skills and ability attribute, are presented [here](/Rules.aspx?ID=3419). _

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

This complex toxin makes the muscles beneath a creature's skin loose and malleable, which fleshwarpers find useful in their work. Rough or jerky movements the victim performs concentrate the toxin in subdermal muscles and eventually cause skin and muscle to slough away.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=274" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 193

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A silver charm bracelet, a _sluggish bracelet_ appears to be a [_bracelet of dashing_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=415), granting you a +1 item bonus to [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) checks. If the curse goes unrecognized, you think you can Activate it to gain a +10-foot status bonus to your Speed for 1 minute. Instead, its activation is as follows.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))    **Effect** You take a –10-foot penalty to your Speed for 1 minute, and the bracelet fuses to you. Thereafter, it grants you no bonus to Acrobatics checks, and it imposes a –5-foot status penalty to your Speed.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

Sleep arrows often have shafts of deep blue or black, and their fletching is exceptionally soft and downy. An activated _sleep arrow_ deals no damage, but a living creature hit by it grows lethargic and must attempt a DC 17 Will saving throw. On a failure, it takes a –5-foot status penalty to its Speeds for 1 round, and is also [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 for 1 round on a critical failure.

**Craft Requirements** Supply one casting of [_sleep_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1675).

---

Slumber wine sees its greatest use in games of intrigue, where an absence can be more devastating than injury. Characters [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38) from slumber wine can't wake up by any means while the poison lasts, don't need to eat or drink while unconscious in this way, and appear to be recently dead unless an examiner succeeds at a DC 40 [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9) check.

**Saving Throw** DC 32 Fortitude; **Onset** 1 hour; **Maximum Duration** 7 days; **Stage 1** unconscious (1 day); **Stage 2** unconscious (2 days); **Stage 3** unconscious (3 days).

May contain spoilers from Outlaws of Alkenstar **Source** [Pathfinder #179: Cradle of Quartz](/Sources.aspx?ID=122) pg. 78 **Price** 600 gp **Usage** worn backpack **Bulk** 2 --- Some mutants savor the acrid smog of Alkenstar and the Gunworks. A _smogger_ recreates this pollution by sucking in clean air and spewing it back out as pungent smog. **Activate** Interact ([poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)) **Frequency** once per hour; **Effect** The _smogger_ creates a 10-foot-radius emanation of smog centered on you, which moves with you. You and other creatures in the smog are [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) while inside the smog, and other creatures are concealed to you and other creatures in the smog. A strong wind doesn't disperse the smog but reduces it to a 5-foot-radius emanation. A creature that must breathe that begins its turn inside of the smog can choose to hold its breath as a free action for the round, but if it doesn't, it becomes [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34). The _smogger_ can maintain this effect for up to 1 minute, and the wearer of the smogger can Dismiss the effect. **Activate** Interact ([poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)) **Frequency** once per day; **Requirements** The _smogger's_ above activation is in effect; **Effect** The smog created by the _smogger_ thickens into a toxic element that burns the eyes, blisters flesh, and causes fits of coughing. All creatures in the smog cloud, including you, must attempt a DC 32 Fortitude save—creatures that must breathe and aren't holding their breath take a –2 circumstance penalty to this save. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is sickened 1.
**Failure** The creature is sickened 1 (or increases their sickened condition value to 2 if it isn't holding its breath). The creature also takes 4d6 poison damage.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the creature takes 8d6 poison damage.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 3"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Smoke Veil](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2609)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=72" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 124

**Price** 60 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn headwear

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

_Smoke veils_ are wigs or headdresses made of flame and ash, giving the wearer a burning coil of fiery hair and concealing their face behind a smoldering, omnipresent haze of smoke and sparking embers. You can use the veil to go unrecognized by hiding your face so that you can attempt [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) without needing a [disguise kit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=19). When you do so, it takes you only 1 minute to create the disguise, and you gain a +1 item bonus to the check. You still need a disguise kit and the full time if you're using cosmetics and other props to change other aspects of your disguise, or if Impersonating a specific person.

**Activate—Blazing Stare** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32))   **Requirements** You dealt fire damage to a target you can see within 30 feet with your most recent action this turn; **Effect** You set your fiery gaze on your target, eyes burning within a cloud of ash and cinder. Roll an [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) check to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=53) the target. Demoralize loses the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16) trait and gains the [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163) trait, and you don't take a penalty when you attempt to Demoralize a creature that doesn't understand your language.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<traits>

**Price** 20 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn eyepiece

</row>

<row gap="medium">

---

These goggles use lenses made out of smoked glass to protect against creatures with gaze attacks. While wearing smoked goggles, you're always considered to be [Averting your Gaze](/Actions.aspx?ID=92), but all creatures have [concealment](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) from you. The fact that the goggles conceal creatures is part of what grants the wearer the item's benefits. If you have a way to negate the concealment from the smoked goggles, you no longer gain the benefit, either.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> concentrate;     **Effect** Until the end of your turn, the blade deals 1d6 extra fire damage instead of just 1. After you use this action, you can't use it again for 10 minutes.

---

Smother shroud robs a victim of distinguishing features, making it difficult for anyone to identify the corpse. Swelling and distention of facial features makes the victim unrecognizable. Increase the DC of any checks made to identify a creature under the effects of smother shroud by twice the stage of the poison. If the victim dies while under the effects of this poison, its corpse retains an inability to take actions with the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16) trait, and if it tries to speak and fails, it counts against responses to the [_talking corpse_](/Spells.aspx?ID=329) spell.

 **Saving Throw** DC 22 Fortitude; **Maximum Duration** 10 rounds; **Stage 1** 2d4 poison damage and [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) (1 round); **Stage 2** 3d4 poison damage, dazzled, a –4 status penalty to Perception checks to hear and smell, and must succeed at a DC 10 flat check to take actions with the auditory trait or the action is lost (1 round); **Stage 3** 4d4 poison damage, [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1), [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=8), unable to smell, unable to take actions with the auditory trait, and [unable to breathe](/Rules.aspx?ID=468)

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Hellbreakers</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #222: Hellbreakers](/Sources.aspx?ID=307) pg. 210

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><row>1 minute ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This padlock exists in a dormant state while it's closed and its associated key is in the keyhole. To activate this item, you remove the key, which causes the keyhole to become a portal to an extradimensional space. This space can hold a single object of up to 1 Bulk by pressing it against the keyhole. At any point within the next 24 hours, the key can be used to open the lock with an Interact action, which safely releases the item onto the ground in your space.

 If the lock isn't opened within the next 24 hours, the key disintegrates, and from then on, a creature who succeeds at a DC 16 Thievery check can [Pick the Lock](/Actions.aspx?ID=2412) open to release the item. On a critical failure, the padlock is destroyed and its contents are lost forever.

This specialized version of a bag of holding appears to be a plain, leather bag that opens at the top, with a thin leather cord attached to cinch the sack closed. The sack's magic allows you to access either its mundane space or an extradimensional pocket. The mundane space inside the sack always holds 5 Bulk. The pocket's capacity varies with the type of sack. Anyone searching the bag can notice a thin, magical seam indicating the existence of the extradimensional space with a successful DC 18 Perception check.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command;     **Effect** You speak a secret command word. Depending on which word you use, the sack either opens up to the mundane sack or the extradimensional pocket. You can Interact to put items in or remove them as normal.

This specialized version of a bag of holding appears to be a plain, leather bag that opens at the top, with a thin leather cord attached to cinch the sack closed. The sack's magic allows you to access either its mundane space or an extradimensional pocket. The mundane space inside the sack always holds 5 Bulk. You can Interact to put items in or remove them as normal. [Smuggling](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2473)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Firebrands](/Sources.aspx?ID=196) pg. 95

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Smuggling involves the discrete transport of people or goods. Examples include moving weapons through a neutral nation to supply a hidden army, transporting endangered creatures out of hostile territory for protection, and dispersing stolen resources to the needy. While smugglers are often associated with illicit substances and illegal activities, Firebrands use smuggling as a way to move people and resources undetected across great distances; they do this by using their own networks or by hiring local experts. Many of the Firebrands' operations involve spectacles as misdirection, and it's not uncommon for them to cause a stir to allow goods to be smuggled more easily elsewhere. In particular, they work with the Bellflower Network to aid in the relocation of displaced peoples across borders.

 Smugglers transport goods by either taking unconventional routes, offering bribes to guards and inspectors, hiding smuggled goods or people, or disguising or declaring the goods as something different. Borders and conflict zones are areas where smuggling thrives, although smaller or more specialized rings can be found all across the Inner Sea region. Smuggling rings typically operate along particular routes or between specific locations, and the availability of smuggling services and the capacity of those services is up to GM discretion.

 The cost of smuggling services depends on distance, as determined by the level of service, and includes transportation fees and a fund for the bribes required to have inspectors look the other way. Level 1 services accept items up to 25 Bulk or a single creature, level 2 services accept items up to 100 Bulk or 3 creatures, level  3 services accept items up to 200 Bulk or 6 creatures, level 4 services accept items up to 300 Bulk or 10 creatures, and level 5 services accept items up to 500 Bulk or up to 20 creatures. More dangerous or difficult subjects of transport, such as explosives or high-level creatures, generally double the cost of the service.

 Smuggling services are generally presumed to succeed. In some cases, the GM might rule that the smuggling could fail, leading to the discovery and possible capture of the goods or people, but GMs are encouraged to warn the players in such cases and offer alternatives, such as paying a higher cost for a more secure smuggling attempt or smuggling the goods themselves.

You can apply snake oil onto a wound or other outward symptom of an affliction or condition (such as sores from a disease or discoloration from a poison). A creature can uncover the ruse by succeeding at a DC 17 Perception check, but only if it uses a Seek action to specifically examine the snake oil’s effects.

For the next hour, the symptom disappears and the wounded or afflicted creature doesn’t feel as if it still has the wound or affliction, though all effects remain. A creature can uncover the ruse by succeeding at a DC 17 Perception check, but only if it uses a Seek action to specifically examine the snake oil’s effects.

This small, crystalline carving takes the shape of a tree leaf and attaches to armor or clothing with a simple strap. **Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 147 **Price** 7,000 gp **Usage** held in 2 hands **Bulk** 1 --- This snare drum and sticks are made from dark wood, and the skin is fine antelope hide. This drum grants you a +2 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=45) checks while playing music with the instrument. **Activate—Prestissimo** ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You play the snare with an extreme cadence. You and all allies within a 30-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) gain the [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=89) condition until the end of your next turn and can use the extra action each round for only [Step](/Actions.aspx?ID=2304) and [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) actions. **Activate—Larghissimo** ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You play the snare with a lassitude that drains the speed from your foes. Enemies within a 30-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) must attempt a DC 34 Fortitude save. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 for 1 round.
**Failure** The creature is slowed 2 for 1 round.
**Critical Failure** The creature is slowed 2 and [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) for 1 round.

These specialized pieces of footwear are designed to distribute the wearer's weight over a larger area to prevent them from sinking while walking on snow. They are typically made with a wood frame and rawhide lacings that are tied over the wearer's other footwear. While wearing snowshoes, you ignore the effects of non-magical difficult terrain caused by snow (reducing greater difficult terrain from snow to ordinary difficult terrain). You take a –10-foot item penalty to your Speed if wearing snowshoes while walking on any surface other than snow.

<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 88

**Price** 550 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These magically enhanced snowshoes are practically a necessity when traversing the gelid tundra and snow-drenched taiga of the Saga Lands. The _snowshoes of the long trek_ allow their wearer to walk across ice and snow with the same surety as dry earth, ignoring the uneven ground and difficult terrain caused by ice and the difficult terrain caused by snow (reducing greater difficult terrain from ice or snow to ordinary difficult terrain). In addition, a character wearing _snowshoes of the long trek_ gains a +5-foot status bonus to their Speed while moving across snow or ice and is never at risk of breaking through naturally-occurring loose or soft snow.

A set of _soaring_ armor helps you fly faster and protects you and nearby allies from falling. While wearing _soaring_ armor, you gain a +10-foot item bonus to your fly Speed, if you have one. As normal, if your fly Speed is based on your land Speed and you already have an item bonus to your land Speed, these bonuses aren't cumulative.

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 134 **Price** 1,900 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** 1 --- A _socialite staff_ is designed as an ornate cane, its metal body glimmering with jewels and gold inlays. A sculpture carved from obsidian tops the head of the staff, its design depending on its wielder's taste. Common choices include birds, flowers, or family crests. While wielding a _socialite staff_, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50) on members of high society. **Activate** Cast a Spell; **Effect** You expend a number of charges from the staff to cast a spell from its list.
  • **Cantrip** [_read the air_](/Spells.aspx?ID=981)
  • **1st** [_charm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=34), [_restyle_](/Spells.aspx?ID=984)
  • **2nd** [_befitting attire_](/Spells.aspx?ID=867), [_phantom crowd_](/Spells.aspx?ID=968)
  • **3rd** [_bottomless stomach_](/Spells.aspx?ID=875), [_shift blame_](/Spells.aspx?ID=997)
  • **4th** _befitting attire_, [_suggestion_](/Spells.aspx?ID=315)
  • **5th** _befitting attire_, _charm_, [_glimmer of charm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=919), _suggestion_
**Craft Requirements** Supply one casting of all listed levels of all listed spells.

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These large portraits are commonly commissioned by secret societies to display their current member ranks, and to protect against members who would break their vows to keep their secrets. Each member being painted gives their consent to be traced by the portrait, and they agree to keep their vows for as long as their membership stands or until death, whichever comes first. This consent can be transferred to a new portrait if one is needed once the society expands, without needing another confirmation.

 Should a member betray the secrets of their society, their image in the _society portrait_ changes within 10 minutes, altering the image of the member by spelling out “TRAITOR” across their form. It provides no details on the specifics of the betrayal. The traitor can attempt a DC 30 Will save or [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) check at the time they betrayed a secret to avoid the portrait revealing their treachery. The traitorous scrawl can be [counteracted](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) by [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78) targeted at the portrait (counteract DC 20, counteract level of 3).

</column>

<traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 39

**Price** 160 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Flintlock Musket](/Weapons.aspx?ID=191)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

---

This _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [flintlock musket](/Weapons.aspx?ID=191)_ features multiple triangular panels that can be folded out of the stock, like the petals of a tigridia flower, that collect sunlight and feed it into the spark gun's core. All damage dealt by a _solar shellflower_ is fire damage.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day (but see below);   **Effect** One of the panels from the _solar shellflower_ detaches and unfurls into a tigridia-shaped construct of flame. For the next 1 minute, whenever you Strike an enemy with the _solar shellflower_, the construct fires a smaller jet of fire that automatically hits the target, dealing 3d4 additional [persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) or twice that on a critical hit. The _solar shellflower_ usually requires a full day to replenish enough solar energy to recharge this Activation, but if used in an environment with especially strong sunlight, such as in a desert, cliff above the clouds, or near the summer solstice, it can recharge in 1 hour instead.

<title

    right="Item 1+"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Soldier's Syrup](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4002)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Myth-Speaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #218: Titanbane
](/Sources.aspx?ID=274) pg. 80

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This thick syrup sweetens potions and creates a distinctive, metallic flavor associated with the festival days in Dhuraxilis. Partygoers are fond of mixing _soldier’s syrup_ with potions to extend their release.

Activating a dose of _soldier’s syrup_ requires you to combine it with another consumable potion that takes 1 action to activate. After swirling the mixture for a few moments, you must either imbibe the augmented potion within 1 minute, or the potion reverts to its unaugmented state. The potion’s level cannot exceed that of the _soldier’s syrup_ it is mixed with, otherwise the syrup is wasted.

When consumed, a _soldier’s syrup_–augmented potion does not immediately grant its benefits to you. Instead, you can activate the potion within the next hour as a single action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait. You can have only one _soldier’s syrup_–augmented potion consumed at a time; consuming a second one renders the first one inert. If you do not activate the potion within 1 hour, the potion spoils inside you, and you become [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) 1 for 24 hours.

---

The blade of this _+2 [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [holy](/Equipment.aspx?ID=299) [glaive](/Weapons.aspx?ID=20)_ shimmers with a prismatic sheen, as if faintly reflecting a rainbow. A _songbird's brush_ sheds [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407) in a 20-foot radius (and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=408) for the next 40 feet). When wielded in combat, the sound of the blade cutting through the air creates a soft, musical trill as if produced by a songbird. Sacred to the faithful of [Shelyn](/Deities.aspx?ID=17), a _songbird's brush_ is so named for the fighting style developed by worshippers of the Eternal Rose, which equates its sweeping swings to painting with a brush. A songbird's brush grants a +2 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks made to dance or sing as long as the glaive is held in two hands.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You sweep the _songbird's brush_ in an arc before you, casting [_prismatic spray_](/Spells.aspx?ID=233) from the glaive. The spell DC is 34. This _prismatic spray_ does not affect good-aligned creatures in its area.

**Craft Requirements** You are a worshipper of Shelyn.

fields.text: Item 15 Songbird's Brush May contain spoilers from Kingmaker Rare Evocation Good Magical Source Kingmaker Companion Guide pg. 84 Price 6,000 gp Usage held in 2 hands Bulk 2 Base Weapon Glaive The blade of this +2 greater striking holy glaive shimmers with a prismatic sheen, as if faintly reflecting a rainbow. A songbird's brush sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius (and dim light for the next 40 feet). When wielded in combat, the sound of the blade cutting through the air creates a soft, musical trill as if produced by a songbird. Sacred to the faithful of Shelyn, a songbird's brush is so named for the fighting style developed by worshippers of the Eternal Rose, which equates its sweeping swings to painting with a brush. A songbird's brush grants a +2 item bonus to Performance checks made to dance or sing as long as the glaive is held in two hands. Activate Two Actions Interact; Frequency once per day; Effect You sweep the songbird's brush in an arc before you, casting prismatic spray from the glaive. The spell DC is 34. This prismatic spray does not affect good-aligned creatures in its area. Craft Requirements You are a worshipper of Shelyn.

Soothing powders are remedies made to stop a particular type of [persistent damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29). Each damage type requires a different formula, with the most popular being bleed soothing powder, poison soothing powder, fire soothing powder, and acid soothing powder. You Activate soothing powder by sprinkling it on yourself or another creature within reach. The target can immediately attempt a new flat check to remove persistent damage the powder works against. Each damage type requires a different formula, with the most popular being bleed soothing powder, [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) soothing powder, [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) soothing powder, and [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524) soothing powder. You Activate soothing powder by sprinkling it on yourself or another creature within reach. The target can immediately attempt a new [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333) to remove persistent damage the powder works against. This powder lowers the DC to 10, as normal for a particularly appropriate type of help.

    level="1"
    right="Item 20"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Sorshen's Scintillating Garment](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5227)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Revenge of the Runelords</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=723" />
<trait label="No Alignment" url="/Rules.aspx?ID=95" />
<trait label="Apex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=532" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=537" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #221: Into the Apocalypse Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=371) pg. 76

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Explorer's Clothing](/Armor.aspx?ID=39)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Perception** +37; [precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=2406) vision 300 feet, [imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=2407) hearing 300 feet, [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59)

**Communication** [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) (Aklo, Azlanti, Chthonian, and Thassilonian)

**Skills** [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) +43, [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) +38, [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) +36

**Int** +6, **Wis** +6, **Cha** +8

**Will** +37 

</column>

---        

The traditional robes of Sorshen, Runelord of Lust, this garment combines a powerful artifact with a sign of office, as with many runelords' accoutrements. Woven of the finest silks and accented with precious stones, the garment is light and easy to move in. Sorshen created, then expanded on the artifact throughout her time as the runelord of lust, adding to it during much of the Age of Legend. This ever-shifting garment of silk and gems subtly reshapes itself in response to its wearer, adopting an appearance most flattering to their form. It's a set of _+3 greater resilient [explorer's clothing](/Armor.aspx?ID=39)_. The garment's four pockets each function as separate _[spacious pouches (type IV)](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3032)_. While wearing the garment, you're immune to [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effects unless you choose otherwise. When you invest _Sorshen's Scintillating Garment_, you increase your Charisma modifier by 1, or increase it to +4, whichever would give you a higher value. 

**Activate—Scintillating Colors** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), aura, [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** _Sorshen’s Scintillating Garment_ casts _dizzying colors_ (DC 41), heightened to 10th rank, to your specifications. If you spend 1 Mythic Point as part of this activation, the spell’s area changes to a 20-foot emanation, and you can designate any number of creatures in that area to be immune to the spell’s effects, and the spell loses the incapacitation trait.

**Destruction** _Sorshen’s Scintillating Garment_ is destroyed if it’s immersed in the waters of a destroyed _Runewell of Lust_.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

fields.text: Item 20 Sorshen's Scintillating Garment May contain spoilers from Revenge of the Runelords Unique No Alignment Apex Artifact Invested Magical Mythic Source Pathfinder #221: Into the Apocalypse Archive pg. 76 Usage worn armor Bulk L Base Armor Explorer's Clothing Perception +37; precise vision 300 feet, imprecise hearing 300 feet, darkvision Communication telepathy (Aklo, Azlanti, Chthonian, and Thassilonian) Skills Arcana +43, Occultism +38, Society +36 Int +6, Wis +6, Cha +8 Will +37 The traditional robes of Sorshen, Runelord of Lust, this garment combines a powerful artifact with a sign of office, as with many runelords' accoutrements. Woven of the finest silks and accented with precious stones, the garment is light and easy to move in. Sorshen created, then expanded on the artifact throughout her time as the runelord of lust, adding to it during much of the Age of Legend. This ever-shifting garment of silk and gems subtly reshapes itself in response to its wearer, adopting an appearance most flattering to their form. It's a set of +3 greater resilient explorer's clothing . The garment's four pockets each function as separate spacious pouches (type IV) . While wearing the garment, you're immune to mental effects unless you choose otherwise. When you invest Sorshen's Scintillating Garment , you increase your Charisma modifier by 1, or increase it to +4, whichever would give you a higher value. Activate—Scintillating Colors Two Actions (arcane, aura, visual) Frequency once per hour; Effect Sorshen’s Scintillating Garment casts dizzying colors (DC 41), heightened to 10th rank, to your specifications. If you spend 1 Mythic Point as part of this activation, the spell’s area changes to a 20-foot emanation, and you can designate any number of creatures in that area to be immune to the spell’s effects, and the spell loses the incapacitation trait. Destruction Sorshen’s Scintillating Garment is destroyed if it’s immersed in the waters of a destroyed Runewell of Lust .

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 23"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Sorshen's Sinuous Guisarme](/Equipment.aspx?ID=5228)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Revenge of the Runelords</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=723" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=537" />
<trait label="Intelligent" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=636" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #221: Into the Apocalypse Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=371) pg. 76

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Guisarme](/Weapons.aspx?ID=380)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

_Sorshen's Sinuous Guisarme_ is a _+4 [mythic striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3500) [keen](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2843) [quickstrike](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2844) [shifting](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2846) [spell reservoir](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2849) [high-grade dawnsilver](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2917) [guisarme](/Weapons.aspx?ID=380)_. The weapon's unique double-bladed design combined with her magical nature grants her the [twin](/Traits.aspx?ID=717) weapon trait. Her spell reservoir rune typically contains [blindness](/Spells.aspx?ID=1453). Her power and intelligence are derived from a magical gemstone containing 13 of Sorshen's dreams, all so outlandish or salacious that most would consider them to be nightmares—although these dreams have been transforming into less horrific visions as Sorshen's changing philosophies continue to influence her weapon. The guisarme can use 3 actions per turn, acting on her wielder's turn. These actions don't count against her wielder's. 

**Activate—Arcane Shift** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You activate the guisarme's _shifting_ rune to Shift Weapon;  **Effect** The guisarme transforms into a [major staff of control](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3039) with 10 charges. If you spend 1 Mythic Point when you Cast a Spell from this staff and expend 10 charges, the spell is heightened to 10th rank, and its Timeflayingsave DC and attack rolls are calculated at mythic proficiency. While in _major staff of control form_, none of the guisarme's weapon runes are active, nor can she Impose Will, but she remains a high-grade dawnsilver item and retains her intelligence—she can use her actions to Cast a Spell from the staff but can't spend Mythic Points to heighten spells to 10th rank. She automatically reverts to guisarme form once all her charges are expended or if you command the staff to revert to guisarme form by using Shift Weapon again. 

**Activate—Impose Will** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Cast a Spell **Frequency** once per day per spell;   **Effect** _Sorshen's Sinuous Guisarme_ casts one of the following spells, heightened to 10th rank, to your specifications: [charm](/Spells.aspx?ID=1463) (DC 45), [flicker](/Spells.aspx?ID=1532), or [subconscious suggestion](/Spells.aspx?ID=1692) (DC 45). The guisarme can use this activation. If you use this activation and spend 1 Mythic Point, the save DC for the spell increases to DC 50.

**Destruction** _Sorshen’s Sinuous Guisarme_ can be destroyed if it’s hurled under the crushing feet of the Oliphaunt of Jandelay, but only if there’s no current runelord of lust living in the world. Note that when Sorshen took on the mantle of ruler of New Thassilon, she abandoned her role as runelord of lust, so at this time, half of this destruction requirement is already fulfilled. Of course, a PC who decides to toss this weapon under the Oliphaunt’s feet during the course of this adventure will likely disappoint—or perhaps even enrage—Queen Sorshen, who might seek retaliation in the future.

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Soul Cage](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1545)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=11" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Negative" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=118" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 51, [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 219

**Price** 1,600 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

As you [Craft](/Actions.aspx?ID=43) your _soul cage_, you trap your soul within it, an integral part of the complicated process of becoming a [lich](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=68). When you're destroyed, your soul flees to the _soul cage_, which rebuilds your undead body over the course of 1d10 days.

 Afterward, you manifest next to the _soul cage_, fully healed and in a new body (lacking any equipment you had on your old body). Only destroying your _soul cage_ can prevent you from returning. You choose the form of your _soul cage_ when you Craft it. A few options include a miniature cage, a ring, an amulet, or a crown. Work with your GM to adjust the usage and Bulk as needed, though a _soul cage_ is rarely more than light Bulk. The _soul cage_ has Hardness 9 and 36 HP.

 If your _soul cage_ is destroyed but you aren't, you can attempt to find your soul and trap it again, building a new _soul cage_. This is no trivial feat and often takes an entire adventure to accomplish. If you don't cage your soul again, you suffer a long decline as described on page 119.

**Craft Requirements** You have [Lich Dedication.](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=179)

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 12"
    pfs="Restricted"
>
[Soul Cage](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4347)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=534" />
<trait label="Void" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=510" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Monster Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=221) pg. 219, [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 51

**Price** 1,600 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This item is crafted by a spellcaster who wishes to become a lich. When a lich is destroyed, their soul flees to the _soul cage_. The soul cage then rebuilds the lich's undead body over the course of 1d10 days. Afterward, the lich manifests next to the _soul cage_, fully healed and in a new body (therefore, they lack any equipment they had on their old body). A lich's soul cage must be destroyed to prevent a lich from returning.

 The standard _soul cage_ is a sealed metal box containing strips of parchment inscribed with magical phrases. This box has Hardness 9 and 36 HP, but some liches devise more durable or difficult-to-obtain _soul cages_. A _soul cage_ might also come in the form of a ring, an amulet, or a similar item; the specifics are up to the creator.
